applies_to: Setra SRCM room condition monitors watching pressure, temperature and humidity in a primary and a secondary room.
summary: The SRCM monitors pressure, temperature, humidity and a user-defined value for a primary and a secondary room, with alarm limits per isolation mode. Its BACnet object list gives the eight readings as analog inputs, alarm limits per isolation mode and input ranges as analog values, display and alarm options as binary values, and input sources, isolation modes and banner modes as multistate values. This is a larger, two-room object list than the single-room Siemens RPM map already in the library.
notes: Object names come from the summary table (pp1-5); read/write comes from the Present_Value row of each object's property table (pp6-35). The property pages print some names differently (e.g. 'Primary Room Isolation Mode' for MV 2).

Twenty Character String Value objects (PCV 1-20: room labels, user-defined names and units, audit trail strings, technical support ID and banner texts) are typed as proprietary objects in the property tables and are left out here.
The list also has notification classes NC 1-4 and event enrollments EE 1-4 for primary and secondary room pressure warning and alarm.
Pressure units follow BV 2 / BV 3 and temperature units BV 4 / BV 10; the analog objects carry no fixed units in the document.
The summary table describes AV 7 as the negative-mode limit; its name and the property page say positive pressure.
The document does not state the data link (BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP).

integration.summary: Read the room pressures (AI 1 / AI 2) and the alarm summary (MV 8 / MI 1) for monitoring. Set the isolation mode of each room (MV 2 / MV 13) and the alarm limits for that mode from the BMS only if the monitor is not configured locally. Temperature, humidity and user values can be written from BACnet when their input source is set to BACnet.

integration.remote_sensors: Temperature, humidity and user-defined inputs can take their value from BACnet: set the matching input source MV (17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27) to 3 = BACnet. The document does not say which object the BMS writes the value to.
setup: The secondary room uses an external transducer on an analog channel (MV 9); set the channel ranges with AV 5 / AV 54 and AV 49-52.
gotchas: Alarm limits exist per isolation mode (positive, neutral, negative) for each room; write the set that matches MV 2 / MV 13.
The analog values carry no fixed units; check BV 2-4 / BV 10 for the active unit before scaling.
Most binary values and several multistate values are display settings; avoid cyclic writes.
